title: Fix CROSSSLOT and nuanced multi-key behavior under a clustered policy
intent: Checks the answer explains CROSSSLOT under a clustered policy, applies hash-tag colocation, and defers nuanced multi-key multi-slot behavior to the enterprise data plane rather than the OSS assumption.
prompt: Review this clustered Azure Managed Redis access pattern and correct the multi-key operations.

input_artifacts.name: access-pattern.txt
input_artifacts.content: policy=clustered (Enterprise); keys: cart:{userA}, coupon:{promoX}, inventory:{skuY}; ops: MGET across all three; a Lua script using KEYS mutating all three atomically; a MULTI/EXEC transaction over all three; assumption: 'multi-key commands always work across the cluster'

embedded_defects.defect: The Lua-with-KEYS script and MULTI/EXEC transaction require all keys in one slot; they are not covered by Enterprise non-atomic scatter-gather and fail across slots. The bare assumption also ignores that OSSCluster would reject even MGET here.
No shared hash tag colocates the co-accessed keys for the atomic and transactional operations that require a single slot.
Assumes generic OSS multi-key behavior instead of the policy-parameterized behavior the enterprise engine enforces.
